cf.title: Reject ADD CONSTRAINT NOT NULL if name mismatches existing domain not-null constraint

input.subject: Reject ADD CONSTRAINT NOT NULL if name mismatches existing domain not-null constraint

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal on master: v1 extends the table rule from commit 96e2af6 to domains, and message #3 confirms the one-constraint rule. standards-compat-1 is about scope, because the entry targets stable branches and no wrong result from the silent success is shown. standards-compat-2 applies only to the v2 NOTICE variant, which departs from the table behaviour. Both points are fixable and need a committer's decision on ERROR versus NOTICE and on back branches.

brief.title: Reject alter domain add constraint not null with a mismatched name
brief.problem: When a domain already has a not-null constraint, `alter domain ... add constraint <name> not null` with a different name succeeds silently today. The author wants the same check that commit 96e2af6 added for tables, so users are not confused about which constraint object enforces the rule.
brief.proposed_design: v1 makes `AlterDomainAddConstraint()` raise an error when the requested name differs from the existing domain not-null constraint name. Unnamed `add not null` and `set not null` stay allowed when repeated. A reviewer's v2 instead keeps the silent success and emits a NOTICE in both `AlterDomainAddConstraint()` and `AlterDomainNotNull()`.
user_visible_surface: v1: new ERROR "cannot create not-null constraint ... for domain ..." with a DETAIL naming the existing constraint, raised by `alter domain ... add constraint <name> not null`.
v2: new NOTICE "Domain ... is already NOT NULL, skipping" for repeated `add not null`, `add constraint ... not null` and `set not null`.
v2: new NOTICE "Domain ... is already NULL, skipping" for repeated `drop not null`.
author_claims: The change aligns domain not-null handling with not-null constraints on tables after commit 96e2af6.
v1 reuses the error code and a similar message from commit 96e2af6, according to Chao Li.
`create domain` needs no change because it already rejects multiple not-null constraints.
Zizhuan Liu claims an ERROR breaks backward compatibility for applications and transaction blocks that rely on silent success.
brief.thread_state: Chao Li and Álvaro Herrera agreed that order-dependent behaviour (unnamed first, then named, fails) is expected. Zizhuan Liu then proposed a NOTICE-only v2; no one has answered it, so ERROR versus NOTICE is still open.
unclear: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches, but the thread does not say whether a new ERROR is acceptable in back branches.
Neither patch touches the documentation, and the thread does not say whether the `alter domain` page needs an update.
v2 changes `drop not null` and `set not null` too, and the thread does not discuss whether that scope belongs in this patch.
The v1 commit message leaves the discussion and CommitFest links blank.

objections.title: New ERROR is proposed for stable branches as a bugfix
objections.failure_scenario: A migration tool re-runs `alter domain d add constraint d_nn not null` on a domain whose not-null constraint has a different name, often the default one. After a minor upgrade the statement raises an ERROR and the transaction aborts. The operator finds out when a deployment that worked last week fails.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix and targets stable branches. v1 turns a statement that succeeds today into an ERROR. Message #4 raises this compatibility cost, and no one has answered it. The thread does not show that the current silent success causes wrong results or corruption, which is what would justify a behaviour change in a minor release.
objections.author_must_show: What wrong result does the current silent success cause that justifies a new ERROR in minor releases, rather than a master-only change?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and v1 turns a statement that succeeds today into an ERROR. Message #4 raises the compatibility cost, and the thread shows no answer and no wrong result from the silent success.

objections.title: v2 NOTICE design makes domains diverge from tables
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs `alter domain d add constraint other_name not null` on a domain that already has a not-null constraint. Under v2 it succeeds with a NOTICE, but the matching table command errors after 96e2af6. Scripts that repeat `set not null` and `drop not null` also start printing NOTICEs on every run.
objections.argument: The stated goal in message #1 is to align domains with tables. v2 in message #4 keeps the name mismatch that 96e2af6 rejects for tables. It also adds NOTICEs to `set not null` and `drop not null`, and the thread does not show that the table forms emit them. That is a second, larger departure from existing practice, and v2 gives no reason for it beyond preserving silent success.
objections.author_must_show: If domains should match tables, why should a mismatched name be accepted with a NOTICE, and do repeated table `set not null` commands emit a NOTICE today?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 states alignment with tables as the goal, and v2 accepts the mismatched name that 96e2af6 rejects for tables. Repeated `alter table ... set not null` emits no NOTICE today, so the added NOTICEs are a second departure that v2 does not justify.

refuted.title: Back-patching a new error changes minor-release behaviour for working scripts
refuted.failure_scenario: A migration script runs `alter domain d add constraint nn1 not null` on a domain that already has a differently named not-null constraint, and today it succeeds. After a minor update that includes v1, the script fails and its transaction rolls back. The user finds out during a routine minor upgrade, which is not the kind of release where users expect this.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix with target version stable, but the thread never discusses back branches. Message #4 shows that silent success is the long-standing behaviour that applications may rely on. A committer would likely accept the ERROR on master for consistency with the table rule, but would hesitate to back-patch a new error where no wrong result or corruption has been shown.
refuted.author_must_show: What incorrect behaviour does the current silent success cause on released branches that justifies a new ERROR in a minor release rather than master only?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. It gives the same scenario and asks the author the same question about a new ERROR in minor releases.

refuted.title: Back-branch target lacks any user report of harm
refuted.failure_scenario: A deployment script repeats `alter domain d add constraint d_nn not null` against a domain whose not-null constraint has a different name. After a minor-release update the statement raises an ERROR and the surrounding transaction aborts. The operator finds out when the routine deploy fails.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix with target version stable, but no message reports a user who was confused or harmed by the silent success. The only stated motive is consistency with commit 96e2af6 (message #1). Message #4 points out that silent success is the current behaviour that existing scripts may depend on. Without a field report, a committer would likely limit a new ERROR to master and would not change minor-release behaviour.
refuted.author_must_show: Which user or bug report shows harm from the current silent success, enough to justify a new ERROR in minor releases instead of master only?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The missing field report is the same gap as the missing wrong result that standards-compat-1 already asks the author to show.

questions: What wrong result does the current silent success cause that justifies a new ERROR in minor releases, compared with a master-only change?
Which behaviour is proposed for commit: the v1 ERROR that matches tables after 96e2af6, or the v2 NOTICE that keeps the mismatched name accepted?
If v2 is preferred, why should repeated `set not null` and `drop not null` on a domain emit a NOTICE when the table forms do not?
Does the `alter domain` documentation page need to state that a named not-null constraint must match the existing constraint name?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera answered the order-dependence question in message #3; the owner needs to know the not-null constraint work for tables and domains in typecmds.c.
committability.liability: A new user-visible ERROR in `alter domain ... add constraint ... not null`; if back-patched, the owner also answers for scripts that break in a minor release.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the visible thread shows no author reply after message #1, and the v2 proposal is unanswered.

priority.reason: The v1 patch is 4.5 KB, touches only typecmds.c and the domain regression test, and follows an accepted table rule. Few users add a named not-null constraint to a domain that already has one, and the open points are the back-branch scope and ERROR versus NOTICE.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so this review cannot confirm that v1 leaves unnamed `add not null` and `set not null` unchanged. Message #4 was judged only from the brief's summary of it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ON UPDATE/DELETE actions on ALTER CONSTRAINT
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends alter table ... alter constraint so it can change the ON UPDATE and ON DELETE actions of a foreign key. It also changes alter constraint to keep the deferrability options the user did not name, and later added an alter constraint ... set variant that changes only the named properties.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the same deferrability syntax should not mean different things depending on the constraint's previous state, and suggested full replacement or a new add or replace constraint command. Wolfgang Walther objected that the SET variant had the same implied-change problem and proposed separate per-action foreign key syntax. The thread reached no agreement on the syntax, and David Steele returned the patch because it had not been updated for over a year and no longer applied.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip collecting decoded changes of already-aborted transactions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Logical decoding checks CLOG when it first decodes a transaction and stops collecting decoded changes for transactions already known to be aborted, so large aborted transactions are not decoded again after a restart or lag. After Andres Freund's review, the revised patch checks transaction status only for large transactions at eviction time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The revised patch did not compile because `logical_replication_mode` was undeclared in `ReorderBufferCheckTXNAbort`. The author posted no new version after this report, so the CF manager returned the entry with feedback. Andres Freund's earlier concerns, misuse of TransactionIdDidAbort() and slow CLOG lookups, were addressed in the design but not decisive.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P4] was withdrawn only because it was merged into another patch, and the thread records no objection to its content. [P8] concerned alter constraint changing foreign key actions. Its state-dependent syntax concern resembles the order dependence raised in message #2, but message #3 settled that point here, and the same rule already applies to tables. The thread cites no earlier discussion of this idea apart from the tables commit it follows.
The order-dependent failure (unnamed first, then named) was settled in message #3, so it is not raised. pg_dump round-trip is unaffected because a domain can hold only one not-null constraint.

Neither v1 nor v2 changes persistent or cross-node state: no new catalog column, WAL record, on-disk format, wire message or exported struct. Both only change whether `alter domain` raises an ERROR or a NOTICE before any catalog write. Back-branch acceptance of a new ERROR is a behaviour question for another angle.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. alter domain still requires domain ownership, and the new ERROR (v1) or NOTICE (v2) shows only a constraint name or the domain name, which the owner can already read in pg_constraint.

Apart from the back-branch question, maintenance cost is small. The change is local to typecmds.c, adds nothing to a hot path, follows the existing table rule, and a committer who knows not-null constraints took part in message #3.

No existing feature, contrib module or extension does this name check for domain not-null constraints, so this angle has nothing to raise. The proposal adds no new mechanism; it extends the table-side check from commit 96e2af6 to domains, so ERROR versus NOTICE and back-branch scope belong to other angles.
For master, the change is a small consistency fix that follows an accepted table precedent, and its cost falls only on users of the command, so demand is not a strong objection there.
